round_log.stdout_tail: The zero-EV admission bar filters noise, not edge: with no margin above costs, no confidence interval on expectancy, and only ~30 signals, "higher net expectancy" is a point estimate indistinguishable from luck—an unmeasurable claim absent a significance test or bootstrap. "No worse maximum drawdown" compares a single-path statistic with huge variance; without a defined tolerance or distributional comparison, near-ties are arbitrary. Reusing the same sealed holdout for every successive challenger burns it via repeated peeking, and there is no multiple-comparison control despite an implied stream of challengers. Finally, nothing specifies how "estimated EV" and "validated state" are computed—if the EV model or validation labels touch the evaluation window, the entire test is lookahead-contaminated before it starts.

round_log.stdout_tail: Proposal: Run one pre-registered, offline exit-research experiment (via `bot/aegis/research/exit_research.py` + ExperimentRegistry, no code/champion changes) testing a fully specified challenger exit — hard stop at −1R, breakeven stop once +1R MFE is reached, and a fixed target at exactly +1R (true 1:1 R-geometry) — against today's early-flatten "quick_win" path, whose `outcome_learning.md` record (n=2517, WR 0.675, payoff_ratio 0.34, expectancy −0.0122, PF 0.77) exemplifies the high-hit-rate/negative-payoff trap Van Tharp dissects via R-multiple expectancy in *Trade Your Way to Financial Freedom*. To make the test causal, replay uses full post-entry OHLC price paths with pre-registered conservative intrabar ordering rules (stop-before-target when both levels touch one bar, worst-case fill within bar, no lookahead), and any exit lacking sufficient archived path data is excluded and counted separately rather than imputed. Costs apply the runner's mandated spread/slippage assumptions as the primary basis, supplemented by a p95 adverse-cost stress band instead of p75-only, since understated tail costs are precisely what let one −0.18R-average loss class erase ~20 typical wins. The hypothesis survives only if sealed-holdout net expectancy has a bootstrap 95% CI excluding zero with PF > 1.0, evaluated per regime stratum and corrected for repeated policy selection (single pre-registered challenger; family-wise adjustment applies if variants are added), and longer holding periods must be re-checked for overnight-gap exposure and unchanged entry/sizing validity. Only a survivor passing every `promote.py` gate may be considered for champion status; all other outcomes are recorded honestly in the registry.
